topic: Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench about 300 km south-west of Guam, is the deepest known point in the ocean at about 10,935 m (2020 survey, ±6 m); Mount Everest is 8,849 m (2020 Nepal–China survey), so its summit would be about 2,086 m under water; pressure exceeds 1,000 atmospheres.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Challenger Deep is a narrow vertical shaft.
myths.reality: It is a slot-shaped depression in the trench floor, several kilometres long; the 'hole' is a long, deep valley, not a well.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

screen_exempt: ^A was right|^B was right|^C was right

landscape.our_gap: Mariana Trench Shorts are side-view infographics or submarine footage; nobody pins the spot on the satellite map, counts the depth down, and actually drops Everest in with the margin stated.

existing.title: How deep is the Mariana Trench?

noaa_deep.title: How deep is the ocean? / Challenger Deep
noaa_deep.notes: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is the deepest known point, about 10,935 m; it lies south-west of Guam.

noaa_pressure.title: How does pressure change with ocean depth?
noaa_pressure.notes: Pressure increases about 1 atm per 10 m; at the bottom of Challenger Deep pressure is over 1,000 atmospheres (more than 8 tons per square inch).

stewart_jamieson.title: The five deeps: the location and depth of the deepest place in each of the world's oceans
stewart_jamieson.notes: Challenger Deep 10,935 ± 6 m (Five Deeps Expedition multibeam survey).

wiki_cd.title: Challenger Deep
wiki_cd.notes: Depth about 10,935 m (±6 m); located at the southern end of the Mariana Trench, about 320 km south-west of Guam; pressure about 1,086 bar.

everest_2020.publisher: Government of Nepal Survey Department / Government of China (joint announcement, 8 Dec 2020)
everest_2020.title: Revised height of Sagarmatha / Mount Everest: 8,848.86 m
everest_2020.notes: Nepal and China jointly announced Everest's height as 8,848.86 m (rounded 8,849 m) on 8 December 2020.

nat_geo_everest.title: Mount Everest is two feet taller, China and Nepal agree
nat_geo_everest.notes: Everest's official height is 8,848.86 m (29,031.7 ft).

worldatlas.title: Challenger Deep: the deepest point on Earth
worldatlas.notes: If Everest were placed in Challenger Deep its summit would still be more than 2 km below the surface.
